title: {{cast.mark}}'s agent reaches {{vocab.resource}} through the gateway, as {{cast.mark}}
goal: {{cast.mark}}'s agent needs to read {{vocab.resource}} in an app that has its own sign-in server, on {{cast.mark}}'s behalf, without a shared service credential and without handing the agent {{cast.mark}}'s own token.
obstacle: The app accepts only tokens its own issuer minted. A shared service account would hide who acted, and {{cast.mark}}'s caller token is not the app's to accept.
control: Ping release claim (2026-11-02), unverified on our tenant: the Privilege MCP gateway, configured with an On-Behalf-Of spec, exchanges {{cast.mark}}'s token for an ID-JAG (leg 1) and, when a Redeem spec with a TokenURL is set, redeems it at the app's own issuer (leg 2). Shown here with in-process mocks.
say: This is a release claim we have not measured on our tenant. The mock shows the shape: the app sees {{cast.mark}}, and no one shares a credential.

steps.title: The agent calls the gateway with {{cast.mark}}'s caller token
steps.tell: The company IdP signed {{cast.mark}} in and issued a caller token for the gateway. The gateway checks it before anything else.
steps.say: The token is for the gateway only. The app never sees it.

steps.title: Leg 1: exchange it for an ID-JAG
steps.tell: The gateway exchanges the caller token at the exchange issuer (RFC 8693). The result is an ID-JAG addressed to the app's issuer (OBO.Resource), with {{cast.mark}} as sub and the calling client in act.
steps.say: The assertion names {{cast.mark}} and says who is acting for them.
steps.why: Delegation is in the token, not in a shared account.

blocked.tell: Point OBO.TokenURL at the partner issuer. It exchanges fine, but the app does not trust it, so leg 2 refuses the assertion.
blocked.say: An assertion from an issuer the app does not trust is worthless.

steps.title: Leg 2: redeem it at the app's own issuer
steps.tell: Only because Redeem.TokenURL is set, the gateway redeems the ID-JAG at the app's issuer (RFC 7523). The app's issuer checks signature, audience, expiry, client and a single-use jti, and mints its own access token for {{cast.mark}}.
steps.say: The app's own issuer decides, and it mints its own token.
steps.why: Without a Redeem TokenURL the exchange result is not redeemed at all.

blocked.tell: Run the replay scenario, or change the audience, or let the assertion expire. Each is refused at leg 2 with the check that failed, and no token is issued.
blocked.say: Expired, replayed, tampered or misaddressed: no token.

steps.title: The app's API sees {{cast.mark}}
steps.tell: The gateway calls the API with the redeemed token. The API verifies it against its own issuer's keys and answers with {{cast.mark}} as the principal.
steps.say: The app logs {{cast.mark}}, not a service account.

blocked.tell: Clear the Redeem TokenURL. The unredeemed assertion goes to the API, which refuses it as not an access token.
blocked.say: A grant is not a key, and the API says so.

steps.title: What the API refuses
steps.tell: The caller's original token is refused (it was not minted by the app's issuer), and so is the raw ID-JAG. Each refusal names the check, from a real request.
steps.say: We show the refusals, not just the happy path.
steps.why: A grant you cannot refuse is not a control.

proof.happy: The API's principal is {{cast.mark}}, the access token is issued by the app's own issuer for the API, and the caller's original token is refused.
proof.blocked: Each of the ten scenarios shows its own refusal at the stage and check that refused it, with no token issued.
